bug_semantics: llama.cpp KV-cache slot/state restore trusts attacker-controlled cell_count from a slot_save_path blob and writes cell_count * row_size bytes into K/V tensors without checking integer wrap of the product or that offset+size fits ggml_nbytes(tensor). In the current sink, llama_kv_cache::state_read_data() (src/llama-kv-cache.cpp) does io.read_tensor(k, sinfo.head() * k_size_row, cell_count * k_size_row) (and the matching V / transposed-V paths, including scatter via sinfo.idxs). A cell_count > cells.size() check exists, but head+cell_count (or a wrapped size) can still write past the tensor buffer, enabling heap overflow from a malicious state file.
flaw_origin: First write is ggml-org/llama.cpp PR #6341 member 662aaea8c9c624f9a6622229e0ed01b7d37248d1 (Jan Boon, 2024-03-27), which added llama_set_seq_data() in llama.cpp. It memcpy'd uint32_t cell_count from the blob (llama.cpp:15231-15233) and called ggml_backend_tensor_set(kv_self.k_l[il], inp, kv_head * k_size_row, cell_count * k_size_row) at llama.cpp:15286 with only a debug GGML_ASSERT(head + cell_count <= kv_self.size). Parent e82f9e2b833d88cd2b30123ef57346c2cb8abd99 has no cell_count * k_size_row seq-restore write. Later refactors (e0dbec0 / b4882 state_read_data rename, 4529c660 scatter fast-path, 0754b7b6 io.read_tensor) carried the same unbounded multiply-and-write; they are not BICs.

reasoning: CVE-2026-43629 is a real, published heap overflow in ggml-org/llama.cpp slot/state restore, not a withdrawn advisory. The GHSA/CVE GitHub reference is the Cyera patches repo, but the vulnerable lines live in llama.cpp. Vulnerability-first search for the first cell_count * k_size_row tensor write (git log -S, then PR decomposition) lands on PR #6341 member 662aaea8, which introduced llama_set_seq_data / --slot-save-path restore. Immediate parent e82f9e2 was fetched and grepped: the seq-restore multiply-write is absent; a pre-existing full-session restore writes from offset 0 and is a different sink. The GitHub squash beea6e1 is a later aggregate of that PR, so it is recorded in decomposed_shas and is not the BIC. Debug GGML_ASSERT and later cell_count > cells.size() do not close wrap or offset+nbytes overflow; Cyera's unmerged patch is the concrete fix. BIC commit-object authorship is human (Jan Boon) with no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI. No upstream fix SHA exists; the finding is confirmed unpatched on llama.cpp HEAD.
remaining_gap: Unpatched on ggml-org/llama.cpp HEAD 3173a56471c1753650cd806694145ffd6dcace67; no merged upstream bounds-check commit. Out-of-tree mitigation is Cyera patches/CVE-2026-43629-kv-cache-overflow.patch and closed PR ggml-org/llama.cpp#24063.

unpatched.reason: Vendor closed ggml-org/llama.cpp#24063 without merging; llama.cpp HEAD still performs unbounded cell_count * row_size writes in state_read_data(). The assigned patches repo only ships an out-of-tree git apply patch.

potential_fix.approach: In llama_kv_cache::state_read_data, compute write_offset/write_size in size_t, reject if write_size / row_size != cell_count or write_offset + write_size > ggml_nbytes(tensor) on every contiguous K/V/transposed-V path, and reject scatter dst_offset + row_size > nbytes before each io.read_tensor.
potential_fix.rationale: That closes both the uint wrap of cell_count * row_size and the head/index-driven write past the allocated KV tensor, which is the heap overflow sink.
